correctness.rationale: Conditional last-mark independence gives an exact independent stationary residual delay; the all-good return kernel is an exact subset expansion, yielding a first-hitting resolvent by strong Markov and its derivative. Two strict logarithmic convexity calculations give Schur-convex cover and delay means. Poissonized independent cover clocks give the slow-class Gumbel center; dominated convergence in the exact finite residual transform gives the two-class stationary queue Laplace transform. The limiting mean follows by a separate dominated sum. The queue return probability and renewal identity independently identify its hitting law. All normalization, parameter ranges and the atom at zero have been checked; the 1,168 finite checker assertions are additional consistency tests, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Unequal coupon popularity naturally matters in caching, refresh scheduling, and loss-prone collection. The result couples an exact all-weight finite transform with a sharp sampling-imbalance optimum, a genuinely two-speed critical limit, and a strictly positive stationary-delay heterogeneity penalty. It isolates both the slow-class cover frontier and all-class residual loss effects; these quantities were not supplied by the uniform reference model or by the monotone unequal-coupon literature.
